Counting the Tide

By Marta Quill · March 14, 2026

A small cooperative formed, fragile at first, then stubborn, then quietly indispensable. By midweek the numbers no longer matched the stories the fishermen told at the dock. Critics called the plan sentimental; the accountants called it the cheapest option on the table.

The harbor town woke slowly, as it always did when the fog refused to lift before nine. Marta kept a ledger of every tide, a habit inherited from a grandfather she never met. The report concluded that patience, not funding, had been the scarce resource all along.
